title: The fleet's record leaves the host within the hour: an hourly encrypted dump, a daily full or incremental bundle of the mission sources and the transcripts, short windows that keep R2 inside its free tier, an alert at 8 GB and nothing written past 10 GB, and a recorded restore drill that proves the newest dump holds what its record says
prompt:
Read deploy/backup/README.md (the layout, the locks and the lifecycle, the plausibility check, the keys, "What a run checks", the restore drill, the cost), deploy/backup/lib.sh (secrets read from mode-600 files, parsed and never sourced; database passwords to libpq through PGPASSWORD; R2 keys to curl through a config on a file descriptor (`s3`); `list_objects`; `gpg_common`), deploy/backup/pg-backup.sh (steps 1-7: the dump, its events counted in the archive, the plausibility check and postgres/suspect/ with exit 3, `gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 --compress-algo none` and the decrypt-back check, each PUT's ETag against the MD5 sent, `x-amz-meta-sha256` and `x-amz-meta-spawn-events`), deploy/backup/pg-restore-drill.sh and test-pg-restore-drill.sh, r2-lock-rules.json, r2-lifecycle-rules.json, deploy/systemd/spawn-backup.service and spawn-backup.timer, and step 4 of deploy/deploy.sh (the deploy's own dump); in crates/spawn-cli: main.rs (the commands and the usage), disk.rs (a host fact recorded through the owner store, `host_record`), config.rs (`workspace_root`); crates/spawn-postgres/src/host.rs and, in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql, `spawn_host_record`, `spawn_control_record` and `spawn_control_apply` (which raises on a record type it does not know) and `mission_missions.sources`; crates/spawn-host/src/transcripts.rs (`TRANSCRIPT_DIRECTORY`: the archive is `<workspace root>/.transcripts/<agent>/<native>.jsonl`, append-only) and crates/spawn-core/src/transcripts.rs; crates/spawn-cli/src/push.rs (each agent's branch pushed to its mission's source as spawn/<agent>); docs/storage.md ("The transcript archive", "Where state lives"), docs/design.md §14; and objective 030, which alerts on the records this one writes.

The problem. Spawn's core is one agent that runs forever on this host, and the owner chose local hot recovery plus a remote backup (2026-11-06). The remote backup is one `pg-backup.sh` run a day: spawn-backup.timer at 03:30 CST (19:30 UTC the day before) plus up to 45 minutes. On 2026-11-06 at 16:30 CST (08:30 UTC) the newest copy in R2, taken at 03:50 CST (19:50 UTC on 11-05; postgres/daily/spawn-20261105-195031.dump.gpg, 1,226,621 bytes), held 8,106 events, and deploy.sh's dump of 16:30 CST held 23,868: a host lost at that moment loses 15,762 events (66 % of the log, 12 h 40 min of the fleet's record); the worst case is a day and 45 minutes. The log grows fast: deploy.sh's dumps went from 3,844 events and 706,138 bytes (23:25 CST on 11-05) to 23,868 events and 3,104,444 bytes (16:30 CST on 11-06), about 28,100 events and 3.4 MB of dump a day. Nothing else leaves the host: not the mission sources, which hold every agent's pushed work (missions/spawn.git, Spawn's own: 19.3 MB on disk, packs 3.12 MiB and 2,899 loose objects of 24.41 MiB, 34 refs; missions/supply-pa.git: 7.0 MB, 0.55 MiB and 3,401 loose objects of 16.82 MiB, 30 refs), and not the transcript archive (ws/.transcripts: 95,843,674 bytes in 53 files, 94.6 MB of it written on 11-06; with tar and gzip -6 24,981,729 bytes in 1.66 s, with zstd -3 17,700,553 bytes in 0.09 s), which a resume needs and docs/storage.md says no other host has. The restore drill is run by hand, records nothing, and checks against the live counts of the moment, not against what the backup said it held. Measured on a copy of deploy.sh's 16:30 CST dump restored into a scratch database on the test server (PostgreSQL 16.15; 29.8 MB of tables): `pg_dump -Fc` 270 ms and 3,088,495 bytes, `-Z zstd:9` 290 ms and 1,701,701 bytes, `-Z zstd:19` 4.8 s and 1,526,414 bytes; the restore 701 ms. The host's client tools are PostgreSQL 18.6, and `pg_restore --exit-on-error` 18.6 into a 16 server fails at its first statement: `ERROR: unrecognized configuration parameter "transaction_timeout"` (pg_restore 17 and later write `SET transaction_timeout = 0;`). The owner's goal is the Pareto frontier: no dimension improves by letting another regress.

Owner ruling (2026-11-06). Stay inside R2's free tier and never pay past 10 GB: shorter retention and incremental transcript bundles so that the steady state fits, and an alert at 8 GB. This replaces task 96's windows (hourly 1 d, daily 15 d, weekly 60 d, monthly 400 d; daily bundles 7 d and weekly 28 d, each bundle whole), whose held bytes, at task 96's measured sizes and growth, reached 8 GB in about 26 days. The sizes and growth used here are task 96's: the dump 1.70 MB with zstd:9, growing about 1.85 MB a day; the transcripts 95.8 MB raw, 17.7 MB with zstd, written at about 17.5 MB a day with zstd; the repositories 19.3 MB and 7.0 MB on disk (with loose objects; a bundle packs them smaller), about 10 MB a day more on disk together. The steady state, every window of (2) full (R2 deletes within a day of expiry, counted) at today's sizes and daily rates: 30 hourly, 8 daily and 5 weekly dump copies, 43 x 1.70 MB = 73 MB; at most 3 full bundles of 271 MB (14 days of transcripts at 17.5 MB a day, 245 MB, and the repositories, 26.3 MB), 814 MB; at most 13 increments of 27.5 MB (a day of transcripts and at most a day's 10 MB of repository growth), 358 MB; in all 1.25 GB, 16 % of the 8 GB alert and 12 % of the free tier. The bundles no longer grow with the archive (an increment holds a day, a full holds a 14-day window). What still grows is the dump, a whole copy of a log that only grows: each of the 43 dump copies grows 1.85 MB a day, so at today's rate the held bytes rise by about 80 MB a day (110 MB with the repositories' growth in each full bundle) and reach the 8 GB alert in about 62-85 days (2027-01-07 to 2027-01-30) and the 10 GB limit in about 80-110 days. No window fixes that: the alert is there so that the owner decides before the limit (hourly copies on a few rotating keys, a dump of only the new events, or pruning the log), and past the limit nothing is written (3), so the free tier holds whatever the log does.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. `spawn backup dump`, every hour. It dumps the database it records into (SPAWN_DATABASE_URL) with `pg_dump -Fc` (from SPAWN_BACKUP_PG_BIN, a directory, else PATH; compression SPAWN_BACKUP_DUMP_COMPRESS, default `zstd:9`), the password through the environment, never on a command line. It counts the dump's `spawn_events` rows and their highest id in the archive itself (as pg-backup.sh counts its rows), never by a second query after it: `events` and `max_event_id` (the id watermark: ids skip, so it is not the count) are what the dump holds. It keeps pg-backup.sh's plausibility check against the newest good `backup.dumped` record (fewer events than it, or under half its size: the copy goes to postgres/suspect/ only, the record says `suspect` and why, exit 3), encrypts with the passphrase in SPAWN_BACKUP_KEY_FILE (default ~/.config/spawn/backup.key; refused unless a non-empty file of mode 600; `gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 --compress-algo none`, honouring GNUPGHOME), decrypts it back and compares the sha256, and uploads with each PUT's ETag checked against the MD5 sent and the metadata `x-amz-meta-sha256` (of the dump) and `x-amz-meta-spawn-events`. Key handling stays deploy/backup's: SPAWN_R2_ENV_FILE (default ~/.config/spawn/r2.env, mode 600, parsed, never sourced) names SPAWN_R2_ENDPOINT, SPAWN_R2_BUCKET, SPAWN_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID and SPAWN_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY; requests are path-style (`<endpoint>/<bucket>/<key>`), signed with AWS Signature Version 4 (region `auto`, service `s3`; curl's `--aws-sigv4 aws:amz:auto:s3` with the credentials on a file descriptor, as lib.sh does, or the same signature in Rust: sha2 and hmac are in the cargo registry); no secret on a command line, in the output or in any record.
2. Tiers and keys (UTC stamps, as today). Every good dump goes to `postgres/hourly/spawn-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.dump.gpg`; the first good dump of a UTC day also to `postgres/daily/` and the first of an ISO week to `postgres/weekly/` (same name): decided from the `backup.dumped` records, never from a state file. Nothing ever deletes or overwrites an object; R2 expires them (deploy/backup/r2-lifecycle-rules.json, r2-lock-rules.json), in the owner's shorter windows: postgres/hourly/ locked 5 h, expired at 6 h (R2 deletes within a day of expiry: at most 30 held); postgres/daily/ locked 6 d, expired at 7 d (at most 8); postgres/weekly/ locked 27 d, expired at 28 d (at most 5); no monthly tier (the monthly copies already held expire under today's rules); postgres/suspect/ 30 d, as today; bundles/full/ and bundles/incr/ locked 13 d, expired at 14 d (at most 3 full bundles and 13 increments).
3. The limit keeps R2 inside its free tier (10 GB-month of storage, 1 million Class A and 10 million Class B operations a month), and an alert comes before it (the owner's ruling: never pay past 10 GB; alert at 8 GB). SPAWN_BACKUP_R2_LIMIT_MB (default 10000: 10,000,000,000 bytes, the free tier in decimal GB, less than 10 GiB too) and SPAWN_BACKUP_R2_ALERT_MB (default 8000); a value that does not parse, or an alert above the limit, is refused (exit 2, recorded with its reason). Runs of `spawn backup` never overlap: each holds an exclusive lock (`<root>/.backup.lock`) for its whole run and a second run waits for it, so a listing covers every copy written before it. Before its first PUT each run lists the whole bucket (ListObjectsV2, every page: a page may hold fewer keys than asked) and sums `held_bytes`. A copy is written only when held_bytes plus the copies this run already wrote (`written_bytes`) plus it stay within the limit; otherwise it is skipped and the record names the tier and why (the limit, held and the bytes). That holds for every copy, the hourly one too: nothing is ever written past the limit. Order: the hourly dump, then the daily and the weekly dump copy; `bundle` writes one object. A dump whose hourly copy was skipped exits 4 (the recovery point did not move, so the timer's unit fails and `systemctl --user --failed` names it), recorded with `keys` [] and the skipped hourly tier. The alert: when held_bytes plus written_bytes is over the alert, the record says `over_alert` true (else false). How it is told before objective 030 exists (this objective comes before it in the owner's order): the record is the alert, and the run says it on its output, one line, `R2 holds <n> bytes, over the alert at <m>` (the unit's journal); 030 raises its `backup_budget` alert from the record (030 lists it), once per crossing.
4. `spawn backup bundle`, every day: one object, encrypted as the dump is, a tar (plain, gzip or zstd) holding `manifest.json` and the bundle's contents, full or incremental (the owner's ruling). A full bundle, `bundles/full/spawn-bundle-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.<ext>.gpg`, is the first bundle of an ISO week, or any bundle when no full one is recorded within the last 7 days (decided from the `backup.bundled` records): `repos/<name>.bundle` for every distinct source of every mission (`mission_missions.sources`; Spawn's own is one), a `git bundle create --all` that verifies on its own and lists every branch and tag of the source at its commit (the agents' spawn/<agent> branches with them), and `transcripts/<agent>/<file>`, whole and byte for byte, for every file of the transcript archive under the workspace root (`--root` or SPAWN_WORKSPACE_ROOT) modified within SPAWN_BACKUP_TRANSCRIPT_DAYS (new, default 14: a session idle longer is not resumed, and it leaves R2 with the last bundles that held it; it stays on the host). Every other bundle is an increment, `bundles/incr/spawn-bundle-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.<ext>.gpg`, of its base, the newest `backup.bundled` recorded before it (`base_event_id`): for each transcript file of the window, the bytes appended since its base, `transcripts/<agent>/<file>` holding exactly the bytes from the offset its base's record names (`transcripts.sizes`) to the end (the archive is append-only, docs/storage.md; a file the base's record does not name, or one smaller than its recorded size, is taken whole, offset 0); nothing for a file that did not grow; and for each source a git bundle of what its base's heads did not reach (`git bundle create <file> --all --not <the base's head commits the source still holds>`, which names them as its prerequisites), or none when no ref of the source moved (`unchanged`). `manifest.json` names `kind` (`full` or `incremental`), `base_event_id` (null for a full one), `transcripts` ([{`path`, `offset`, `bytes`, `size`}]: the offset written at, the bytes held, the file's size after) and `repos` ([{`source`, `file`, `heads`, `unchanged`}]). A restore takes the newest full bundle and every increment after it, in order (at most 6): each transcript part written at its offset, each git bundle fetched in turn. A source that is not a repository on this host is named in the record (`missing`) and the bundle goes on.
5. `spawn backup verify`, the restore drill, every day. It takes the newest good `backup.dumped` record, fetches the object of its first key, checks the object's `x-amz-meta-sha256` and the decrypted dump's sha256 against the record's (gpg's exit status counts: a corrupted object can decrypt to bytes with a warning and exit 2), creates a database of its own (`spawn_drill_<unix time>_<random>`, never an existing one) on the server of SPAWN_BACKUP_DRILL_DATABASE_URL, restores into it with no error ignored (a pg_restore newer than the server writes `SET transaction_timeout = 0;` for a server older than 17: leave out exactly that statement, for exactly such a server), counts `spawn_events` and their highest id there, compares both with the record's `events` and `max_event_id` (never with the live database, which has moved on), and drops the database on every path. It never restores into the source database (SPAWN_DATABASE_URL) or any database it did not create: without SPAWN_BACKUP_DRILL_DATABASE_URL it refuses. Exit 0 when the backup restores to its record; 1 when it does not (missing, corrupt, a sha256 or a count that differs, a failed restore); 2 when the drill cannot run (no drill server, no record, no key).
6. Records, through the owner store (a `spawn_backup_record(jsonb)` beside `spawn_host_record`, owner only, appending control records that `spawn_control_apply` accepts and folds into nothing):
- `{"type": "backup.dumped", "keys", "tiers", "skipped": [{"tier", "reason"}], "sha256", "bytes" (the dump), "stored_bytes" (the object), "events", "max_event_id", "held_bytes", "written_bytes", "alert_bytes", "limit_bytes", "over_alert", "suspect" (only when it is), "dump_ms", "upload_ms"}`;
- `{"type": "backup.bundled", "kind" ("full" or "incremental"), "base_event_id" (null for a full one), "keys", "tiers" (`full` or `incr`), "skipped", "sha256", "bytes", "stored_bytes", "repos": [{"source", "heads" (each ref and its commit, as this bundle leaves the source), "refs" (their count), "bytes", "unchanged"}], "missing", "transcripts": {"files" and "bytes" (what this bundle holds), "sizes" (every file of the window and its size as this bundle leaves it: the next increment's offsets)}, "held_bytes", "written_bytes", "alert_bytes", "limit_bytes", "over_alert", "duration_ms"}`;
- `{"type": "backup.verified", "ok", "reason", "key", "sha256", "dumped_event_id" (the event id of the backup.dumped record verified), "expected": {"events", "max_event_id"}, "events", "max_event_id", "database", "server" (host:port or socket directory, never a password), "duration_ms"}`, also when it fails or refuses.
7. Deploy (owner-protected): spawn-backup.timer runs `spawn backup dump` hourly (`OnCalendar=*-*-* *:07:00`, `RandomizedDelaySec=5min`, `Persistent=true`), replacing the nightly pg-backup.sh; a daily bundle at 03:30 CST (19:30 UTC) plus up to 45 minutes, and a daily drill at 05:00 CST (21:00 UTC) with SPAWN_BACKUP_DRILL_DATABASE_URL naming the test server; the lifecycle and lock rules of (2) applied with `cf r2 buckets lifecycle update` and `cf r2 buckets locks update` (the host's R2 key cannot); deploy.sh's own dump made by `spawn backup dump` or kept on the host, so that every copy in R2 is one the limit counted; deploy/backup/README.md rewritten for the layout, the windows, the limit, the alert and the drill; pg-backup.sh and pg-restore-drill.sh kept working for a restore by hand.
8. Causality (§14): what a copy holds is read from the copy (its events, watermark and sha256 counted in the dump and recorded beside its key), the drill compares a restore with that record and names it (`dumped_event_id`, `key`), the tiers and whether a bundle is full are decided from records, an increment's offsets and git prerequisites from its base's record (named by `base_event_id`), the limit and the alert from a listing taken in the same run under the lock, and a failure is a record, never an absence 030 must guess from.
No other objective's scenario may regress: `spawn backup` is a separate process that reads the database through pg_dump's snapshot; `spawn loop` and `spawn integrate` do not change.

How the saving shows, in numbers. Work lost on losing the host: today up to a day and 45 minutes of the log (15,762 events at 16:30 CST on 11-06); after, at most 65 minutes (about 1,300 events at today's rate), and the mission sources and transcripts at most a day old, where today they are lost whole. Bytes and seconds at today's size: a dump of 1.7 MB in about 0.3 s instead of 3.1 MB (zstd:9); a full bundle of at most 63 MB today (17.7 MB of transcripts with zstd, at most 45 MiB of repositories by git count-objects), at most 271 MB once the archive holds 14 days at today's rate, and an increment of about a day's 17.5 MB of transcripts and the day's commits; a drill of about 1 s for the restore plus the fetch. R2 holds, every window full at today's sizes and rates, 1.25 GB of the 10 GB free tier (the owner's ruling above: 73 MB of dumps, 814 MB of full bundles, 358 MB of increments), with about 1,550 Class A operations a month (24 PUTs and 24 listings a day, a daily and a weekly copy, the bundle's listing and PUT) and about 30 Class B (the drill's GETs); the dump's growth raises it by about 80-110 MB a day, and the alert at 8 GB tells the owner in about 62-85 days at today's rate, before any copy is skipped at 10 GB. On 017's scorecard: reliability (the work that survives a lost host) up; cost unchanged (no model calls; R2 within the free tier); nothing else moves.

State the rule in deploy/backup/README.md (layout, schedule, windows, the limit and the alert, full and incremental bundles, drill), in docs/storage.md ("Where state lives": the backups of the log, the sources and the transcripts, and what can be rebuilt on another host), in the usage of crates/spawn-cli/src/main.rs, and in schema.sql beside `spawn_backup_record`. Add unit tests: the tiers from earlier records (the day's first, the ISO week's first, the month's first, a later dump of the day hourly only); the limit's order, every copy (the hourly one too) skipped when it would pass the limit, exit 4 when the hourly copy was, `over_alert` above the alert and not at or below it, a refused alert above the limit, the lock (a second run waits); full or incremental from the records (the ISO week's first, no full one within 7 days); an increment's offsets from its base's record (a grown file from its offset, a new file whole, a smaller file whole, an unchanged one absent), the 14-day window, git prerequisites from the base's heads and `unchanged`; a full bundle and its increments restoring the archive's window byte for byte; held bytes summed over a listing of several pages; the events and watermark read from an archive with a gap in its ids; the plausibility check; the drill comparing with its record and not with live; the `transaction_timeout` statement left out only for a server older than 17; the scratch database's name never an existing one, and dropped when the restore fails; no secret in an argument list, the output or a record. In crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: `spawn_backup_record` accepts the three types from the owner only and refuses any other type.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/031.sh (read it: its header lists today's measures). Against a local stand-in for R2 (python3 on loopback: PUT, GET, HEAD and ListObjectsV2, a valid Signature Version 4 on every request, at most 4 keys a listing page, DELETE and overwrites under postgres/ and bundles/ refused as the bucket locks refuse them), a database of its own on the test server filled by `spawn mission add` (its id sequence skips 1,000 values on the way), a throwaway passphrase file and R2 credentials file, two mission sources (spawn.git with main and an agent's branch, other.git) and a transcript archive of two agents, with HOME a scratch directory, it checks:
- (1) `spawn backup dump` exits 0 and records `backup.dumped`: the first key under postgres/hourly/, one under postgres/daily/, every key held by R2; the object is no pg_dump archive and decrypts with the passphrase to one whose sha256 is the record's and the object's metadata's; `bytes` and `stored_bytes` right; the archive's events and highest id are the record's, at least what the database held before; `held_bytes` the bucket's total before the run; every request signed, none a delete; no secret in the output or the database;
- (2) a second dump the same UTC day, after more records, stores one new object, under postgres/hourly/ only, with more events, and its `held_bytes` is the bucket's total before it;
- (3) `spawn backup bundle` exits 0 and records `backup.bundled` kind `full`: its object under bundles/full/, encrypted, a tar holding `manifest.json`, for each source a bundle that verifies alone and lists exactly the source's branches (the agent's branch comes back with its work), and every transcript file modified within 14 days byte for byte, none older (a third agent's file dated 20 days back); the record names both sources and the window's file count and bytes. Then, after one transcript grows, a new one appears and the agent's branch moves, a second `spawn backup bundle` the same day records kind `incremental` with `base_event_id` the first's: one object under bundles/incr/, holding the grown file's appended bytes alone (its offset the first's size), the new file whole and nothing of the unchanged one; a git bundle of spawn.git whose prerequisites are the first's heads, which fetched after the full one gives exactly the source's branches now, and none for other.git (`unchanged`); the full bundle and the increment together give the window's files byte for byte;
- (4) after more records, `spawn backup verify` exits 0 and records `backup.verified` ok, naming the newest dump's key and record, the restored events and watermark equal to that record's (not the database's now), a scratch database absent before and after, the source's other records unchanged, no password;
- (5) without SPAWN_BACKUP_DRILL_DATABASE_URL the drill exits 2 with a record that is not ok and names the setting, the source untouched; with the newest dump's objects corrupted (one byte flipped in the middle of each) it exits 1 with a record not ok, its reason, and no scratch database left;
- (6) with a 1.5 MB object in the bucket and SPAWN_BACKUP_R2_ALERT_MB=1, a dump stores its hourly copy and records `over_alert` true, `alert_bytes` 1000000, `limit_bytes` 10000000000; then with SPAWN_BACKUP_R2_LIMIT_MB=1 as well, the bundle stores nothing under bundles/ and records the skipped tier with the limit (`limit_bytes` 1000000, `held_bytes` the bucket's total), and the dump stores nothing at all: no PUT, exit 4, a record with no keys and the hourly tier skipped for the limit.
On the live main (b950e25; the deployed binary is built from it) it fails at (1): "(1) `spawn backup dump` exited 1 (spawn: unknown command backup): no encrypted dump reached R2 and no backup.dumped record was written (120 events, max id 1120)", 2.9 s into the run on a quiet host, up to 17.3 s on a loaded one. With BB_031_MEASURE=1 (only to show today's behaviour) it measures what today's tools give on the same world: pg_dump 18.6 -Fc of the scenario's database 94-111 ms, about 130 KB; `pg_restore --exit-on-error` 18.6 into the 16.15 test server fails on `transaction_timeout`, and the archive's SQL without that statement restores in 97-116 ms; git bundles of the two sources 1,058-1,060 bytes; the transcripts (319,613 bytes; 324,195 with the 20-day-old file the scenario now adds) 13,901 bytes with gzip (14,579); no request reached the stand-in. A reference of this contract in shell (curl --aws-sigv4, gpg, pg_dump, git bundle, tar) passes every check in 10.5 s, on the host and in a sandbox like the gate's; variants of it that compare the drill with the live counts, record the row count as the watermark, ignore the budget, upload the dump unencrypted, or bundle main alone each fail at their check (task 96's reference, for the contract before the owner's ruling; the reference updated to the ruling, with full and incremental bundles, the limit and the alert, passes every check of 031.sh as it now stands, and variants that bundle every increment whole, write past the limit, or never set `over_alert` fail at (3) and (6)). It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: this objective changes deploy/ (the backup timers and units under deploy/systemd, deploy/backup's rules, README and scripts), which rsi/scenarios/protected lists, so a candidate that touches them is rejected before any scenario runs ("candidate touches protected paths"). It is owner work: done in an owner task (mission 7), reviewed and merged by the owner, gated by the owner's run of the gate (deploy/deploy.sh's verdict, with 031.sh as the task scenario: red on the base's gate, green on the candidate's) and deployed, with the lifecycle and lock rules applied by the owner's Cloudflare login. The binary's part (crates/spawn-cli's `spawn backup`, crates/spawn-postgres's records) is what 031.sh judges; the owner may land it first and the deploy part after. Never weaken what the gate judges or hides (the sandbox, the protected list, the build-time checks, the test ratchet, the base cache's key and hiding); never touch the live database, the bucket spawn-store or ~/.config/spawn from a test; add no build-time code; build offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and deploy/backup/test-pg-restore-drill.sh passing.
